text: With the Spring launch about ten weeks out, Theo writes one Terraform configuration: a resource group, a virtual network and subnet, an Azure Container Registry, and an AKS cluster named aks-driftwood-prod -- four resources, with Terraform working out the create order from the references between them.

A helm_release resource installs the storefront app's chart onto that cluster in the same terraform apply, fully in code, exactly matching Casey's ask: no separate manual Helm step for anyone to forget.

The chart's values-prod.yaml needs an autoscaling floor and ceiling. Sizing that from scratch means guessing at traffic Driftwood hasn't seen yet, so Theo reuses a template a former colleague shared from a much higher-traffic retail client's engagement: minReplicas 10, maxReplicas 20.

It's a known-good, battle-tested starting point, not a careless guess -- with a mental note to right-size it once there's real traffic data. That note competes with everything else still ahead of launch, and doesn't make it onto a ticket.

Nothing in terraform plan's output calls minReplicas 10 unusual -- it's a valid value that simply guarantees ten pods run around the clock, no matter how little traffic the app actually sees. Lesson 5 builds the pipeline that will deploy this exact configuration automatically.
